articles.title: More than the Score - Was an action-packed Wafcon a good sign for African women's football? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: The 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations was full of shocks and surprises
articles.body:
World Service , · 26 Aug 2026 , · 29 mins

The build-up to the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations was chaotic, with short-notice changes to qualification and even the dates of the tournament itself. But once the action got under way, it was packed with shocks and surprises. Cameroon scored upset wins over Nigeria and Morocco on their way to their first-ever Wafcon title, with star-making performances from the likes of Monique Ngock and Michaely Bihina. Malawi also had a fairytale run to the final, fuelled by goals from the Chawinga sisters. But does this changing of the guard mean a brighter future for African's women football? Sophia Hartley talks to journalists Busisiwe Mokwena and Biola Solace-Chukwu about the big takeaways from this year's Wafcon, and what's next for the players and teams that made their names at the tournament. Unexpected questions and beyond the scoresheet chat. More than the Score tells stories from all over the world of sport. From Formula One to netball, MMA to figure skating, and Grand Slam tennis to Diamond League athletics. We've got interviews with extraordinary athletes, as well as the experts working behind the scenes, from football super-agents to the coaches keeping athletes in peak form. Plus, we've got the expertise of the BBC's top journalists, who share their insights from decades of covering sport at all levels. articles.title: Acidente entre motos e caminhão causa lentidão em avenida de Sorocaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Congestionamento atingiu os dois sentidos da Avenida J.J. Lacerda, que foi liberada por volta das 9h10. Motociclistas tiveram escoriações.
articles.summary: Um acidente entre duas motos e um caminhão causou lentidão na Avenida José Joaquim de Lacerda, na zona norte de Sorocaba (SP), na manhã desta quarta-feira (26).
articles.body:
Um acidente entre duas motos e um caminhão causou lentidão na Avenida José Joaquim de Lacerda, na zona norte de Sorocaba (SP), na manhã desta quarta-feira (26).

Conforme apurado pela TV TEM , as motos estavam paradas no semáforo quando foram atingidas pelo caminhão. Segundo testemunhas que estavam no local, elas foram parar debaixo do caminhão após a batida.

Houve congestionamento nos dois trechos da avenida, em um dos principais acessos para a zona norte da cidade e para quem deseja ir para o Parque das Águas. A pista foi liberada por volta das 9h10.

Segundo apurado pela TV TEM, os motociclistas tiveram escoriações e foram socorridos com ferimentos leves.

articles.standfirst: Região pode registrar chuvas entre 20 e 30 mm/h ou até 50 mm/dia, com ventos intensos que variam de 40 a 60 km/h e queda de granizo.
articles.summary: Cidades podem registrar chuvas entre 20 e 30 mm/h ou até 50 mm/dia, com ventos intensos que variam de 40 a 60 km/h e queda de granizo.
articles.body:
Inmet emite alerta de tempestade para cidades do Sul do Rio e Costa Verde — Foto: Divulgação/Inmet

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) divulgou nesta quarta-feira (26) um alerta amarelo , que significa perigo potencial, de tempestade para as 24 cidades do Sul do Rio e Costa Verde. O aviso começou à 00h e vai até às 23h59 desta quarta-feira (26).

De acordo com o instituto, as cidades podem registrar chuvas entre 20 e 30 mm/h ou até 50 mm/dia, ventos intensos que podem variar entre 40 e 60 km/h e queda de granizo. Além do baixo risco de corte de energia elétrica, estragos em plantações, queda de galhos de árvores e de alagamentos.

O aviso é válido para as cidades de Angra dos Reis (RJ), Barra do Piraí (RJ), Barra Mansa (RJ), Engenheiro Paulo de Frontin (RJ), Itatiaia (RJ), Comendador Levy Gasparian (RJ), Mendes (RJ), Miguel Pereira (RJ), Paracambi (RJ), Paraíba do Sul (RJ), Paraty (RJ), Paty do Alferes (RJ), Pinheiral (RJ), Piraí (RJ), Porto Real (RJ), Quatis (RJ), Resende (RJ), Rio Claro (RJ), Rio das Flores (RJ), Sapucaia (RJ), Três Rios (RJ), Valença (RJ), Vassouras (RJ) e Volta Redonda (RJ).

articles.title: #SouManaus 2026: Cadastro de informais termina nesta quarta (26) | G1
articles.standfirst: Cadastro segue até quarta na Semacc, com exigência de documentos e foto para participação no festival.
articles.summary: O cadastro para o #SouManaus 2026 exige documentos e foto na sede da Semacc para trabalhadores informais que desejam atuar no festival em setembro.
articles.body:
Primeira noite do Sou Manaus Passo a Paço 2025 — Foto: Semcom

O cadastramento de trabalhadores do comércio informal que querem atuar no festival “#SouManaus Passo a Paço 2026” segue nesta quarta-feira (26), das 8h às 14h, na sede da Secretaria Municipal de Agricultura, Abastecimento, Centro e Comércio Informal (Semacc), no bairro São Francisco. O evento será realizado nos dias 4, 5, 6 e 7 de setembro.

O cadastramento busca organizar os trabalhadores informais e garantir planejamento, ordem e segurança durante o festival, considerado um dos maiores eventos culturais de Manaus.

Segundo o secretário da Semacc, Moisés Cunha, a ação é uma oportunidade para valorizar os trabalhadores e movimentar a economia local.

“São mais de mil famílias beneficiadas, direta e indiretamente, por meio do comércio informal. O ‘#SouManaus’ vem para fortalecer esse comércio, valorizar quem trabalha e movimentar a economia da cidade”, disse Cunha.

Os interessados devem levar cópias do RG, CPF, comprovante de residência e uma foto 3x4 dentro do prazo e horário definidos.

Quem pretende vender alimentos terá atenção especial. A Subsecretaria de Gestão de Vigilância Sanitária (Visa Manaus) vai oferecer um curso sobre o manuseio correto dos produtos para garantir a segurança alimentar durante o festival.

O curso vai orientar os vendedores sobre boas práticas de higiene e manipulação, contribuindo para que o público tenha acesso a alimentos seguros durante o evento.

articles.title: Lixão a céu aberto vira alvo de novo pedido do MPMG contra Governador Valadares | G1
articles.standfirst: Vistoria encontrou lixo acumulado sobre o solo, chorume, resíduos em curso d’água, mau cheiro e animais na área de transbordo.
articles.summary: Vistoria encontrou lixo acumulado sobre o solo, chorume, resíduos em curso d’água, mau cheiro e animais na área de transbordo.
articles.body:
Lixão a céu aberto vira alvo de novo pedido do MPMG contra Governador Valadares — Foto: MPMG/Divulgação

O Ministério Público de Minas Gerais (MPMG) pediu à Justiça medidas mais rigorosas contra a prefeitura de Governador Valadares após uma área de transbordo de resíduos no bairro Turmalina se transformar em um lixão a céu aberto. A vistoria realizada pelo órgão no dia 14 de agosto encontrou grande quantidade de lixo acumulado e uma série de problemas ambientais e de segurança no local.

Entre os pedidos feitos à Justiça está o aumento da multa diária aplicada ao município, de R$ 1 mil para R$ 5 mil. O MPMG também quer que a penalidade seja estendida ao prefeito e que ele apresente, em até cinco dias, medidas concretas para regularizar a área e o serviço de destinação dos resíduos.

Segundo o Ministério Público, o problema se agravou depois que o contrato com a empresa responsável por transportar os resíduos até o aterro licenciado de Chonin de Cima terminou , em fevereiro deste ano. Até a vistoria de agosto, uma nova empresa ainda não havia sido contratada.

Com isso, grandes volumes de resíduos permaneceram acumulados na área de transbordo durante cerca de seis meses. Na fiscalização, o MPMG encontrou lixo depositado diretamente sobre o solo, sem impermeabilização ou sistema de drenagem para a água da chuva.

Também foram identificados problemas no controle do chorume, líquido produzido pela decomposição dos resíduos. Parte do lixo estava próxima ou em contato com um curso d’água. A vistoria registrou ainda forte mau cheiro e a presença constante de aves, cães e cavalos.

O cercamento da área também apresentava falhas e fazia divisa com residências. Catadores trabalhavam no local em condições consideradas precárias e sem equipamentos de proteção individual.

Município já pagou mais de R$ 1 milhão em multas

O caso é acompanhado pelo MPMG há quase duas décadas. Os pedidos atuais fazem parte de uma ação judicial iniciada em 2008 para cobrar o cumprimento de um Termo de Ajustamento de Conduta (TAC) firmado entre o município e o Ministério Público em 2006.

Entre as obrigações assumidas pela prefeitura está a implantação de um local devidamente licenciado para a destinação final dos resíduos sólidos.

MPMG pede medidas mais duras contra Valadares após área virar lixão no Turmalina — Foto: MPMG/Divulgação

Segundo o MPMG, o município já pagou mais de R$ 1 milhão em multas pelo descumprimento de decisões judiciais relacionadas ao caso. Para o órgão, porém, as penalidades financeiras não foram suficientes para resolver o problema, que se agravou ao longo dos anos.

Além do aumento da multa, o Ministério Público pediu que a prefeitura comprove a contratação de uma nova empresa para transportar os resíduos, regularize ambientalmente a área de transbordo e conclua o diagnóstico dos serviços de limpeza urbana contratado pelo município.

O MPMG também quer que o Plano de Gerenciamento de Resíduos de Serviços de Saúde (PGRSS) seja aprovado pelos órgãos competentes.

Para os promotores Marco Aurélio Romeiro Alves Moreira e Mariana Cristina Pereira Melo, a situação demonstra um problema estrutural e prolongado na gestão dos resíduos de Governador Valadares. O órgão aponta riscos para os moradores que vivem no entorno, para os trabalhadores que atuam na coleta de materiais recicláveis e para o meio ambiente.

O Ministério Público informou ainda que está atualizando o cálculo das multas já vencidas. O valor poderá ser cobrado em uma nova ação judicial.

O caso continua sendo acompanhado pelo MPMG, que afirma que seguirá cobrando do município o cumprimento das obrigações ambientais.

O g1 entrou em contato com a prefeitura de Governador Valadares e aguarda posicionamento.

articles.title: Equatorial Maranhão alerta para impactos das queimadas na rede elétrica | G1
articles.standfirst: No primeiro semestre de 2026 a Distribuidora já registrou 233 ocorrências provocadas por queimadas
articles.summary: No primeiro semestre de 2026 a Distribuidora já registrou 233 ocorrências provocadas por queimadas
articles.body:
Com o início do período de seca e estiagem no Maranhão, a Equatorial Maranhão faz um alerta para as queimadas próximas à rede elétrica, já que as ocorrências envolvendo essa prática tendem a aumentar. Apesar de ainda ser utilizada por algumas pessoas para a limpeza de terrenos e no controle da vegetação, a prática das queimadas pode sair do controle e causar graves consequências.

Quando realizadas próximas à rede elétrica, as chamas e o calor intenso podem danificar cabos, postes e outros equipamentos do sistema de distribuição, provocando interrupções no fornecimento de energia, além de representar riscos à segurança da população, dos animais e de quem realiza a queima.

Somente de janeiro a junho de 2026, a Equatorial Maranhão registrou 233 ocorrências na rede elétrica provocadas por queimadas e incêndios em vegetação , número 8,9% superior ao registrado no mesmo período de 2025, quando foram contabilizadas 214 ocorrências .

Somente de janeiro a junho de 2026, a Equatorial Maranhão registrou 233 ocorrências na rede elétrica provocadas por queimadas e incêndios em vegetação. — Foto: Divulgação/Equatorial

No ranking dos municípios com maior número de ocorrências em 2026, estão:

São Luís, com 58 ocorrências (2.868 clientes interrompidos); São José de Ribamar, com 27 ocorrências (1.681 clientes interrompidos); Imperatriz, com 24 ocorrências (3.098 clientes interrompidos); Santa Inês, com 15 ocorrências (1.078 clientes interrompidos); Timon, com 9 ocorrências (1.141 clientes interrompidos); Pinheiro, com 6 ocorrências (1.154 clientes interrompidos).

Embora São Luís tenha registrado o maior número de ocorrências, Imperatriz foi o município com o maior número de clientes afetados , com 3.098 interrupções no fornecimento de energia decorrentes de queimadas e incêndios em vegetação.

Segundo dados do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (INPE), de janeiro a agosto deste ano, o Maranhão registrou mais de 3,5 mil focos de calor. No cenário nacional, até o momento, o estado ocupa a 4ª posição no ranking de ocorrências, atrás apenas de Mato Grosso, Tocantins e Pará, o que acende o alerta, já que os casos tendem a se intensificar entre os meses de agosto e outubro.

De acordo com o Executivo de Segurança do Trabalho da Equatorial Maranhão, Gabriel Vieira, durante o período de estiagem é fundamental redobrar os cuidados para evitar esse tipo de incidente. "Mesmo que uma queimada se inicie de forma aparentemente controlada, a situação pode tomar maiores proporções em poucos minutos. A combinação de altas temperaturas, baixa umidade do ar, ventos fortes e vegetação seca favorece a rápida propagação das chamas, aumentando significativamente o risco de incêndios de grandes proporções. Por isso, a orientação é que a população evite qualquer tipo de queima em áreas próximas à rede elétrica e acione imediatamente o Corpo de Bombeiros ao identificar um foco de incêndio", destaca Gabriel.

Além dos riscos à segurança e ao fornecimento de energia, as queimadas provocam sérios impactos ambientais. O fogo destrói a vegetação nativa, compromete a biodiversidade, causa a morte de animais silvestres e contribui para a degradação do solo. A fumaça liberada também reduz a qualidade do ar, agravando problemas respiratórios, especialmente entre crianças, idosos e pessoas com doenças crônicas.

Nunca descarte cigarros ou fósforos acesos, principalmente em áreas com vegetação. — Foto: Divulgação/Equatorial

Para prevenir acidentes com queimadas, a Equatorial Maranhão reuniu algumas dicas importantes:

• Não queime lixo, principalmente perto de postes e da rede elétrica; • Nunca descarte cigarros ou fósforos acesos, principalmente em áreas com vegetação; • Não faça fogueiras próximas à vegetação e às plantações; • Não utilize o fogo como ferramenta para limpeza de pastagens; • Utilize aceiros como barreiras preventivas; • Priorize alternativas como a roçada com ferramentas ou máquinas; • Siga as orientações dos órgãos ambientais para reduzir o risco de propagação das chamas.

Em caso de incêndio nas proximidades da rede elétrica, a população deve acionar o Corpo de Bombeiros, pelo número 193, e a Equatorial Maranhão, pela Central de Atendimento 116.

A Equatorial Maranhão reforça que essas orientações integram o Movimento “Vc+ Seguro” , iniciativa que atua de forma preventiva, orientando seus clientes e reforçando a importância da segurança com energia elétrica para evitar acidentes. A campanha tem como objetivo ampliar o acesso à informação e conscientizar a população sobre os riscos e perigos relacionados ao uso da energia elétrica, reafirmando o compromisso da Distribuidora com a segurança, a prevenção de acidentes e o bem-estar da comunidade.

Durante o mês de agosto, as ações do movimento ganham reforço com a campanha Agosto Vermelho, iniciativa promovida pela Associação Brasileira de Distribuidores de Energia Elétrica (Abradee), voltada à conscientização da população sobre os riscos de acidentes envolvendo a rede elétrica.

articles.title: Terremoto raso pode ter contribuído para deslizamentos no Nepal | G1
articles.standfirst: USGS registrou tremor de magnitude 4,4 na região da fronteira entre Nepal e Tibete pouco antes da inundação que devastou vilarejos.
articles.summary: USGS registrou tremor de magnitude 4,4 na região da fronteira entre Nepal e Tibete pouco antes da inundação que devastou vilarejos.
articles.body:
Um terremoto de magnitude 4,4, com epicentro a 10 quilômetros de profundidade, foi registrado pelo Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS) na região de fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, na China, pouco antes da enchente repentina que atingiu a área nesta quarta-feira (26). O desastre deixou mortos e desaparecidos.

Autoridades locais não estabeleceram, até o momento, uma relação direta entre o tremor e o rompimento que atingiu o rio Bhote Koshi — mas a proximidade temporal entre os dois eventos chamou atenção e é um dos pontos apurados nas investigações que começam agora.

De acordo com o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS), o tremor foi registrado às 8h37 da manhã. Minutos antes de as imagens de segurança registrarem a avalanche que arrasta gelo e rochas que atingem a passagem de terra entre os dois países.

Uma combinação de imagens de satélite mostra os vales perto da fronteira entre o Nepal e a China em 25 de agosto de 2026, antes das inundações devastadoras (T), e em 26 de agosto de 2026, após o desastre (B). — Foto: Reuters

A suspeita é de que o tremor tenha desencadeado uma avalanche de gelo e rochas no rio Lhende Khola, do lado nepalês, provocando as inundações.

A região havia passado por intensas chuvas antes, que estava congeladas e represadas. Com o tremor, esse gelo foi rompido e a água liberada com intensidade. Isso explica a enchente repentina na região, sem que qualquer órgão ambiental pudesse prever.

De acordo com especialistas, o que chama atenção no tremor registrado nesta manhã é a profundidade: a 10 quilômetros esse é considerado um terremoto raso.

➡️ Quanto mais próximo da superfície é o foco de um tremor, menos distância as ondas de choque percorrem até chegar ao solo e às construções, e menos energia se dissipa no caminho. Na prática, isso significa que a força da trepidação chega quase intacta à superfície, atingindo o que está ao redor com mais intensidade.

Parte do gelo e das rochas que se desprenderam no rio Lhende Khola não desceu completamente — formou um novo bloqueio mais acima, no curso do rio, antes de chegar às áreas já atingidas.

Esse tipo de barreira funciona como uma represa improvisada: a água continua se acumulando atrás dela até que a pressão seja suficiente para rompê-la de novo, liberando outro volume repentino de água e detritos rio abaixo. É esse cenário que as autoridades monitoram agora.

O risco também não fica restrito ao Nepal. O Lhende Khola nasce nas montanhas do Himalaia e desce em direção às planícies, alimentando outros rios que atravessam a fronteira até a Índia. Por isso, alertas de cheia foram emitidos nos estados indianos de Bihar e Uttar Pradesh — regiões que ficam a centenas de quilômetros do ponto do desastre, mas que recebem a água que desce da cordilheira.

articles.title: Justiça suspende empréstimo de aposentada analfabeta | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher de 80 anos foi convencida por telefone de que receberia restituição do INSS. Contrato foi feito por biometria facial, sem testemunhas, o que contraria exigências legais para analfabetos.
articles.summary: Mulher de 80 anos foi convencida por telefone de que receberia restituição do INSS. Contrato foi feito por biometria facial, sem testemunhas, o que contraria exigências legais para
articles.body:
A Justiça determinou a suspensão dos descontos de um empréstimo no benefício previdenciário de uma aposentada de 80 anos, em Natal. A decisão, em caráter liminar, foi obtida pela Defensoria Pública Cível após a mulher, que é analfabeta, ser induzida a erro.

Segundo a ação, a aposentada recebeu uma ligação de uma suposta instituição financeira. A pessoa informou que ela teria valores a receber referentes à restituição de descontos associativos contestados no Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS). A mulher acreditou que se tratava da devolução de um dinheiro que já lhe pertencia.

A contratação do empréstimo ocorreu de forma eletrônica, por meio de biometria facial. O processo foi feito sem assinatura a rogo ou a presença de testemunhas. A legislação civil exige essas formalidades para negócios jurídicos firmados por pessoas que não sabem ler nem escrever.

Ao analisar o pedido, a Justiça destacou a grande vulnerabilidade da consumidora devido à idade avançada e ao analfabetismo. O juízo ressaltou que a biometria facial não substitui as exigências legais para contratos com analfabetos. O entendimento segue decisões reiteradas do Tribunal de Justiça do Rio Grande do Norte (TJRN) em casos semelhantes.

A decisão judicial apontou a fragilidade da operação. O valor do empréstimo foi sacado integralmente no mesmo dia, com desconto simultâneo de seguro prestamista. Não há registro de que a mulher tenha recebido os esclarecimentos adequados sobre o contrato.

Para evitar o comprometimento da subsistência da aposentada, a Justiça determinou que o banco suspenda imediatamente as cobranças mensais. A instituição também está impedida de incluir o nome da mulher em cadastros de proteção ao crédito, sob pena de multa diária em caso de descumprimento.

A Defensoria Pública orienta que pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade fiquem atentas a contatos telefônicos que ofereçam 'restituições' ou 'devoluções de valores' vinculados ao INSS ou a bancos. O órgão recomenda buscar orientação antes de comparecer a agências ou assinar documentos, inclusive em formato eletrônico.

Ação foi movida pela Defensoria Pública do Estado do Rio Grande do Norte, DPERN — Foto: Cedida/DPERN

articles.title: Chuva cancela desfile cívico para aniversário de Campo Grande | G1
articles.standfirst: Cancelamento foi informado pela prefeitura por volta das 7h30; bolo de 32 metros será montado a partir das 10h e cortado às 11h na Avenida Afonso Pena.
articles.summary: Cancelamento foi informado pela prefeitura por volta das 7h30; bolo de 32 metros será montado a partir das 10h e cortado às 11h na Avenida Afonso Pena.
articles.body:
Chuva cancela desfile cívico de aniversário em Campo Grande — Foto: Magno Lemes

A chuva que atingiu Campo Grande na manhã desta quarta-feira (26) provocou o cancelamento do desfile cívico em comemoração aos 127 anos da capital de Mato Grosso do Sul. Apesar do cancelamento, a distribuição do bolo de aniversário está mantida.

A Prefeitura de Campo Grande informou o cancelamento do desfile por volta das 7h30, por meio das redes sociais.

“Devido à forte chuva, o desfile está cancelado”, informou a prefeitura.

Mesmo sem o desfile, o Sistema S do Comércio de Mato Grosso do Sul informou, em nota, que a população poderá participar da distribuição do bolo de aniversário.

A montagem no local está prevista para começar às 10h, e o corte oficial do bolo deve ocorrer às 11h.

Com 32 metros de comprimento, o bolo será distribuído à população na região central de Campo Grande, na Avenida Afonso Pena, entre a Avenida Calógeras e a Rua 14 de Julho.

A receita leva cerca de 1,4 mil ovos e recheio de doce de leite. O bolo terá a inscrição “CAMPO GRANDE 127 ANOS” em letras grandes e deve ser suficiente para atender mais de 2 mil pessoas.

A produção também envolve uma grande quantidade de ingredientes e cuidados especiais para o preparo, armazenamento e transporte.

Depois de pronto, o bolo precisa ser mantido protegido e sob controle de temperatura até chegar ao local da distribuição.

O doce de leite foi escolhido para o recheio por ser um sabor conhecido e associado à memória afetiva das comemorações.

Para reduzir o uso de materiais descartáveis convencionais, serão utilizados pratos e garfos ecológicos.

articles.summary: Avalanche atingiu região da fronteira e engoliu vilas inteiras. Autoridades já registram 384 desaparecidos, a maioria turistas estrangeiros. Itamaraty ainda não disse se há brasileiros no local.
articles.body:
Uma inundação repentina e devastadora deixou mortos, desaparecidos e muita destruição em vilas na região da fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete, na China, nesta quarta-feira (26).

Um levantamento preliminar do Conselho de Turismo do Nepal identificou 384 viajantes, incluindo 291 estrangeiros e 93 cidadãos nepaleses, que foram reportados como desaparecidos nas áreas afetadas. Entre os países com cidadãos desaparecidos estão:

A agência de notícias sul-coreana Yonhap informou separadamente que cerca de oito cidadãos do país também estavam desaparecidos no Nepal . O Itamaraty ainda não disse se há brasileiros no local.

As informações estão sendo verificadas e conferidas em coordenação com agências de viagem, guias, autoridades locais e órgãos de segurança.

Estrada alagada após uma enchente repentina em Galchhi, distrito de Dhading, no Nepal — Foto: REUTERS/Stringer

I magens transmitidas pela televisão mostram casas destruídas pelas águas da enchente, carros flutuando e uma ponte de metal sendo levada pela correnteza do rio Bhote Koshi

Testemunhas contaram à agência de notícias Reuters que as águas engoliram vilarejos inteiros.

No condado de Gyirong, no Tibete, um deslizamento atingiu uma passagem de terra entre os dois países. Há vários desaparecidos, entre eles oito sul-coreanos que trabalhavam em uma usina hidrelétrica.

Segundo a agência de notícias oficial chinesa Xinhua, ele ocorreu no lado nepalês e atingiu o porto local, interrompendo estradas, comunicações e fornecimento de energia na região de Shigatse.

O distrito montanhoso de Rasuwa, no Nepal , que tem uma população de cerca de 50 mil habitantes, foi um dos locais mais atingidos. Helicópteros de resgate não conseguiram pousar nas áreas afetadas.

"Há devastação por toda parte. Os assentamentos próximos ao rio foram completamente destruídos. Cinco dos meus parentes estão desaparecidos", disse Tula Bahadur BK, uma profissional de saúde em Rasuwa, à Reuters.

O primeiro-ministro do Nepal , Balendra Shah, afirmou que policiais e militares estão se unindo aos esforços de resgate.

A causa da inundação ainda não está clara , mas uma enchente similar no mesmo rio, no ano passado, foi posteriormente atribuída ao esvaziamento de um lago glacial.

articles.title: Cockroaches, 87kg expired sweets: FSSAI slaps notices on Delhiâs JW Marriott, Andaz over hygiene lapses
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Food regulator FSSAI has issued notices to five-star hotels JW Marriott and Andaz at Delhiâs Aerocity over serious food safety and hygiene .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Food regulator FSSAI has issued notices to five-star hotels JW Marriott and Andaz at Delhiâs Aerocity over serious food safety and hygiene violations, including active cockroaches near freezers, expired food, poor sanitation and improper storage practices, officials said on Wednesday.The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it issued a notice to Juniper Hotels Pvt Ltd, which operates the Andaz hotel at Aerocity, after an inspection uncovered "serious food safety violations".A separate notice was issued to JW Marriott, a unit of Aria Hotels and Consultancy Services Pvt Ltd, over "serious food safety violations and non-compliance with FSSAI requirements."The regulator said food samples had been collected from both establishments and further action would depend on laboratory reports.87kg expired sweets, cockroaches found at AndazDuring the inspection at Andaz, FSSAI said several serious food safety and hygiene deficiencies were detected, including improper segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, pest activity, poor sanitation, inadequate food-handler hygiene and improper food storage.Officials found expired food products, including around 87 kg of expired sweets, an expired cake base and bread packets.Other deficiencies included inadequate temperature monitoring, improper allergen segregation, poor waste management, structural and maintenance issues and inadequate supplier verification and receiving practices.The inspection team also collected regulatory and surveillance samples of cow ghee, veg mayonnaise, creamy coconut milk powder, honey twigs, yellow masoor dal, tomato sauce, orange marmalade and coconut cookies for laboratory analysis.FSSAI said inspectors found active cockroaches near freezers, houseflies, mosquitoes in the grinding room and spider webs. A 'gutka' packet was also found inside the bottling plant area.Inspectors also detected duplicate date-marking on expired bread packaging, along with severe unpleasant odours.The regulator said chillers were situated directly between two bathrooms, with exhaust venting into the chiller section.FSSAI has directed the hotel company to take immediate corrective action on the violations and submit a compliance report at the earliest, along with supporting evidence.Food safety inspections across DelhiThe latest action follows inspections at two major hotels in Aerocity that had earlier revealed a range of hygiene and food-safety issues, including cockroaches, flies, foul smell, expired food and deficiencies in the segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian items.At one of the hotels, inspectors found deficiencies in food segregation and recorded complaints regarding cockroaches, flies and foul smell."Deficiencies were found in the segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food in the kitchen. Complaints regarding cockroaches, flies and foul smell were recorded," said sources."Some bread packets bearing expired stickers were also found. Around 87 kg of expired sweets were found in the confectionery area and were destroyed on the spot. In the pastry section, expired cake bases, flies and cockroaches were found," they added.At another Aerocity hotel, an inspection that continued for around two days recorded 59 deficiencies."The inspection continued for around two days, during which 59 deficiencies were recorded," said sources.Officials also found that some food products did not have the required FSSAI licences or endorsements. Irregularities were detected in the labelling of packaged food products.Mouldy apples and rotten tomatoes were found, while several food items were stored in the open. Deficiencies were also noted in vegetarian and non-vegetarian food storage.Cockroaches and broken containers were found in the bakery section, sources said.FSSAI enforcement driveThe inspections are part of a wider enforcement drive by FSSAI against food business operators and e-commerce platforms over food safety violations, misleading claims, labelling and advertisements.In a separate case earlier this month, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in Maharashtra suspended the FSSAI licence of a prominent establishment at Kranti Chowk in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar with immediate effect.The action followed a surprise inspection under the "Safe Food Safe Maharashtra" campaign, which uncovered serious hygiene violations and public health concerns.Inspectors found chopped paneer with a foul smell stored in the kitchen for cooking without any validity or use-by date.Spoiled paneer poses a serious risk of rapid microbial growth because of its high moisture and protein content, officials said.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: India, China could help Trump resolve Iran crisis through diplomacy: Hillary Clinton
articles.summary: US News: Former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton has said India and China could play a key role in helping resolve the escalating Iran crisis, urging Pres.
articles.body: Former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton has said India and China could play a key role in helping resolve the escalating Iran crisis, urging President Donald Trump to pursue âdiplomacy instead of blusterâ.In an interview with C-SPAN, Clinton said China and India could exert influence on Tehran because of their economic and energy ties with Iran.âIf you want to figure out how Trump could get out of this, I think the key to it is probably China and India, because if you look at who buys the most oil and gas from Iran, it's China and India,â Clinton said.India, China could pressure TehranClinton said China, in particular, could use its position as one of Iranâs biggest oil and gas buyers to pressure Tehran over the ongoing crisis.âChina is far ahead of that; they have been banking a lot of fossil fuels they got in tankers ... they have been building more reserves ... but they are going to need Iran,â she said.Clinton argued that economic leverage from countries such as China and India could offer Washington a diplomatic route to de-escalate the conflict.âIt does seem to me that's where the best pressure would come from if Trump were willing to actually use diplomacy instead of bluster,â she said.Strait of Hormuz remains key flashpointThe Strait of Hormuz remains at the centre of the crisis, with disruptions to shipping threatening a major global energy route. Nearly a fifth of the world's energy supplies passed through the Gulf chokepoint in normal times.Clinton said she would use the threat of secondary sanctions against China to push Beijing to persuade Iran to reopen the strategic waterway and restore the previous situation.âI would certainly tell the Chinese I was unless they were going to help us to try to get the Iranians to open the Strait of Hormuz and try to go back at least to the status quo ante,â she said.US steps up sanctions pressure on IranClinton's remarks came as the Trump administration intensified economic pressure on Tehran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a fresh round of sanctions targeting Iran and warned countries doing business with the Islamic Republic to sever their financial ties or face US retaliation.Tehran has threatened to respond militarily to Washington's expanded sanctions, while Iran has also signalled willingness to resume talks.China, Turkiye and the UAE are among Iran's largest trading partners. Pakistan, Oman and Qatar have also been involved in efforts to mediate between Washington and Tehran.Clinton, however, specifically identified India and China as countries that could help put pressure on Tehran because of their energy ties with Iran.Trump threatens 'crushing economic operation'The latest escalation follows Trump's August 20 warning that he would launch what he called the âmost crushing economic operationâ against Iran if Tehran failed to reach a deal.Clinton also criticised what she described as strategic miscalculations surrounding the conflict, saying the decisions that led to the current crisis had failed to deliver the political outcome Washington sought.She said greater involvement by countries with strong economic ties to Iran could provide an alternative to further military escalation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Plastic nurdles wash up on Hartlepool and North Yorkshire beaches
articles.summary: Plastic nurdles are washing up on beaches more than 30 miles south of the Port of Tyne spill site.
articles.body:
Nurdles are washing up on beaches more than 30 miles (48km) south of the source of a spillage of millions of plastic pellets.

Tonnes of the pieces of plastic, known as nurdles, washed up across north-east England after a crash between two vessels at the Port of Tyne damaged two shipping containers.

The nurdles have now been spotted on beaches in North Yorkshire and Teesside, and volunteers are worried the clean-up effort is being "left to communities" and called for a "long-term plan".

The Port of Tyne said its response had not been "scaled back" and it continued to maintain the same level of on-water resource as throughout the clean-up operation.

The port said during the recent high tide period it had temporarily increased the number of boats and operatives deployed.

North East mayor Kim McGuinness said her team had contacted Solis Marine, the company organising the clean-up on behalf of the shipping insurers, to ask them to commit to responding to new nurdle deposits and asking why casual workers had been stood down.

She said: "They should not be allowed to decide on their own what a proper clean-up looks like.

"Our local volunteers have given up their time and worn themselves out combing beaches."

Solis Marine has been approached for comment and a Port of Tyne spokesperson said the response continued to be guided by Ambipar, experts in environmental spill response.

"We remain committed to removing as much material from the river as possible within that expert guidance," they said.

Environmental charity Fidra, which runs the Great Nurdle Hunt project, said nurdles were highly mobile and they would continue to wash up in the north-east of England and beyond in the months and years to come.

A spokesperson said: "There needs to be a long-term plan and resources to monitor and respond when nurdles wash up in the future.

"The continued spread of nurdles to regions far from the source of the spill vividly highlights the wide reaching impact - volunteers are reporting new finds every day."

The charity called for regulation and international maritime organisation rules for pellet loss prevention and preparedness plans.

Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council officers have inspected beaches from Marske to Redcar and confirmed nurdles had been found.

Currently, the authority said they were "concentrated in relatively small pockets".

"Teams are also looking to organise targeted beach clearance days, where volunteers can support the clean-up effort," a spokesperson said.

"In addition, we are exploring the use of appropriate mechanical equipment to help expedite the removal process, where this can be undertaken safely and without causing damage to the coastline or sensitive habitats."

Senior scientist at the National Oceanography Centre Dr Charlotte Williams said tides were highly predictable and tidal currents generally move water back and forth.

"Floating material such as nurdles would be transported by a combination of processes, including tides, winds, waves and larger-scale coastal currents," she said.

"Wind, and the surface currents can be really variable and are often more important for moving floating material than the back-and-forth motion of the tide alone."

Durham County Council confirmed its officers had been carrying out daily patrols along the coast and "a very small number" of pellets were found on Monday morning.

Head of environment for the county council, James Gilchrist, said: "We will continue to monitor the situation alongside partner agencies and should there be a need for a clean-up that volunteers can take part in, we will publicise details of this."

articles.title: German airport worker dies of malaria after 'mosquito arrives on plane'
articles.summary: Five other airport workers are also receiving treatment following the rare outbreak at German's busiest airport.
articles.body:
A Frankfurt Airport worker has died of malaria after a rare outbreak led to six employees contracting the serious infection spread by mosquitoes.

It is believed the mosquitoes arrived at Germany's busiest airport on a plane, according to German public health officials.

The remaining five infected individuals are receiving medical treatment, a spokesperson for airport operator Fraport said.

Traps have been installed at the airport and mosquitoes captured will be analysed in a laboratory to determine their species and origin.

"Sadly, we must confirm that one employee has died as a result of the infection," the Fraport spokesperson told the BBC.

"We have provided comprehensive information to all employees and encourage them to consult a doctor if they experience any symptoms."

It was reported in July that the outbreak involved four infected workers.

The Robert Koch Institute - a German federal government agency and research institute for disease control and public health - previously said the four employees fell ill between 4 and 6 July and the mosquitoes were brought in by plane.

The institute said malaria in Germany almost exclusively affects long-haul travellers who were infected in malaria-endemic areas, and that malaria transmitted within a German airport is rare.

"The lack of a travel history can lead to a delayed diagnosis. A delayed diagnosis increases the risk of a severe course of the diseases," the institute said in its epidemiological bulletin.

The last case of airport malaria was in 2023 also at Frankfurt Airport, it added.

The BBC has contacted Frankfurt Public Health Department, who is leading the investigation into the outbreak, for comment.

Malaria is a disease spread by some types of mosquitoes biting humans, and is mostly found in tropical countries, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

The infection, which is preventable and curable, is caused by a parasite and does not spread from person to person. However symptoms can be mild or life-threatening.

articles.title: Middlesbrough murder investigation as two people die in house fire
articles.summary: Cleveland Police says it "cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime" after the fire near Middlesbrough.
articles.body:
A murder investigation has been launched after two people died in a house fire.

The blaze in Grangetown, Middlesbrough, broke out just before 05:30 BST and also left a woman in hospital in a critical condition, alongside a further three people who suffered non-life threatening injuries.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating what had happened but was "keeping an open mind and cannot rule out any links to wider organised crime at this time".

The fire happened about two miles from the A66 crash that killed five young men and two police officers on Saturday morning.

Redcar and Cleveland Local Policing Commander Supt Emily Harrison said the force was working to "establish the circumstances of exactly what has happened".

"We will have a high visibility presence in the Grangetown area as this investigation progresses, and to provide reassurance to local communities, who will no doubt be impacted by this tragic incident."

Patrols have been increased in the local area to "reassure the local community", the force said.

Firefighters damped down the smoking roof of the home which has been wrecked by the fire.

A ladder was propped against a rear upstairs window of the family home.

A neighbour, who asked not to be named, said: "My daughter heard shouting and screaming this morning.

The neighbour said a family lived at the house, adding: "I don't know the people who live there, we just say hello when we walk past."

Police officers guarded a cordon around the scene and Northern Powergrid staff were also on site.

Cleveland Fire Brigade said it sent six fire engines and the Incident Command Unit to the scene.

A spokesperson said road closures were in place in the surrounding area and asked members of the public to avoid the area where possible.

Redcar MP Anna Turley said the community had faced a "profound amount of heartbreak over the past few weeks".

She said: "I am devastated to hear of the tragic loss of life following this morning's fire in Grangetown.

"My deepest condolences are with the families, friends and loved ones of those who have died, and my thoughts are also with those injured and receiving treatment."

Grangetown councillor Adam Brook urged people not to speculate.

He said: "Many residents have been in touch with me throughout the morning, and I know there is understandably a great deal of concern.

"However, I would urge people not to speculate or share unconfirmed information."

The families of the people involved have been informed and they are being supported by specialist officers.

articles.title: From Kanganaâs âbikiniâ barb to GIVA pulling ad: How Kriti Sanonâs Raksha Bandhan row unfolded
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A jewellery advertisement featuring actor Kriti Sanon ahead of Raksha Bandhan has snowballed into a wider debate over clothing, culture and wo.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A jewellery advertisement featuring actor Kriti Sanon ahead of Raksha Bandhan has snowballed into a wider debate over clothing, culture and womenâs freedom.The advertisement soon drew criticism from BJP MP Kangana Ranaut, a response from Sanon, backing from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and, finally, the withdrawal of the campaign by jewellery brand GIVA.The controversy centred on GIVAâs Raksha Bandhan campaign featuring Sanon in an Indo-Western outfit comprising a bralette-style blouse, cape and draped skirt.While the advertisement was intended as a festive campaign, its styling triggered criticism online.Some social media users questioned whether Sanonâs outfit was appropriate for a Raksha Bandhan advertisement and also pointed to the absence of traditional elements associated with the festival.Kanganaâs âbikiniâ remark sparks rowThe controversy gained momentum after actor-turned-politician Kangana Ranaut aimed the advertisement in an Instagram Story.Ranaut questioned why a woman would tie a Rakhi while wearing what she described as a bikini or undergarments, arguing that women today have a wide range of clothing options.âItâs a wonderful time to be a woman. Our closets are full of a variety of clothes; todayâs woman is a global woman,â Kangana wrote.She went on to list options ranging from cocktail dresses and lehenga cholis to jeans, saris, bikinis and salwar kameez, before asking why one would choose such an outfit while tying a Rakhi.Calling the advertisement âintentionally creepyâ, Ranaut questioned the way the festival had been portrayed.The criticism added fuel to an already active online debate, with some users also questioning why traditional elements such as a puja thali and tilak were absent from the campaign.âCulture & traditions are in her heart, not her necklineâ: Kriti hits backSanon subsequently responded to the criticism, though she did not name Ranaut directly.In an Instagram post, the actor said the essence of a festival was not determined by the clothes a person wore but by the emotions and meaning attached to the tradition.She described Raksha Bandhan as a bond of protection and said she and her sister tie Rakhi to each other, adding that they pray for each otherâs âhealth, happiness & long lifeâ.Sanon also explained that the same sentiment extended to their dogs, whom they considered family.The actor then broadened her response beyond the advertisement itself, questioning why women continued to be told what to wear.She said ethnic fashion had evolved, but a womanâs respect for her culture was still being judged by her clothes.Her post ended with the line, âCulture & Traditions are in her heart, not her neckline!âRahul Gandhi enters debateThe controversy then took a political turn after the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, came out in Sanonâs support.Gandhi said a womanâs clothing, actions and movements were her own choices and urged people to stop trolling women for exercising their freedom.âWhat a woman wears, what she does and where she goes - is her choice,â Gandhi said in an Instagram post. âStop trolling women for exercising their freedom.âHis intervention shifted the conversation further from the advertisementâs styling to the broader question of whether womenâs clothing should be used as a measure of their cultural values.GIVA pulls advertisementAs the controversy continued, GIVA announced that it had withdrawn the advertisement from all media.In a statement shared on Instagram, the jewellery brand said it had the âhighest regard and deep respectâ for Indian culture, traditions and festivals.The company said it had intended to celebrate the festive occasion with families and had sought to extend that celebration to pets as well.GIVA said that if the advertisement had inadvertently hurt the sentiments of some sections of society, that was never its intention.âOut of respect, we have withdrawn the said advertisement from all media,â the brand said.It concluded its statement by wishing people âlove & positivityâ during the festive season.A festive ad turns into a larger debateThe episode has since moved beyond the advertisement itself.The exchange between Kangana and Sanon has opened up a larger debate over how women dress during festivals, who gets to define cultural appropriateness and whether clothing can be used to judge a woman's respect for tradition.What began as a festive jewellery campaign eventually turned into a public debate involving actors, politicians and the brand itself.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Prince Harry and Meghan land in UK days after announcing move
articles.summary: Prince Harry, Meghan, and their two children are believed to have flown into the country privately from California.
articles.body:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in the UK, BBC News understands.

Prince Harry, Meghan and their children Archie and Lilibet are believed to have flown into the country privately from California, and landed in Birmingham shortly before midday.

A spokesman for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex said "this is not something we would comment on".

There did not appear to be a police presence as Harry and his family left the airport, a source told the BBC.

Last week, it was reported that the couple would be relocating to the UK in August. They will not return to official duties but will live in Britain as non-working royals.

It is thought the family will base themselves at a private property outside of London in the Cotswolds area.

Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in school and the new term is due to start next week.

The Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.

King Charles was told of the move earlier this month. The family visited the King at his Highgrove home in July this year, but it is understood the move was not discussed.

Before that visit, Prince Harry and Meghan had not been in the UK together since they attended the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022.

Charity? Acting? The Cotswolds? What will Harry and Meghan's UK life look like?

The Prince and Princess of Wales have also been informed of their plans.

The Sussexes' security in the UK has been the subject of debate since the news of their return broke.

Last year, Prince Harry lost a legal challenge over the levels of security he and his family are entitled to while in the country.

The duke had sought to overturn a decision that had downgraded his security after he stopped being a working royal and moved to the US.

It is unclear what provisions will be made for their security in the UK and who will pay for it.

After the announcement of the Sussexes' intended return, a Home Office spokesperson said decisions on the security of royals were taken by the Executive Committee for the Protection of Royalty and Public Figures (Ravec), and the UK government's protective security system was "rigorous and proportionate".

Prince Harry has previously said that worries about safety have prevented him from coming to the UK and bringing his wife and children.

Last month, the duke and six other public figures lost their High Court privacy case against the publisher of the Daily Mail and Mail.

They face paying up to Â£34.5m to Associated Newspapers in legal costs.

articles.title: 9 common myths about wrinkles debunked — and what dermatologists want you to know instead
articles.summary: From the importance of genetics to whether $200 moisturizers are a good buy, here's the whole truth and nothing but the truth.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

I once read about a lady who didn't smile for over 40 years . Her reason for such a stationary expression was not a distaste for joy and laughter, but something else entirely — to prevent wrinkles . She'd decided that maintaining a straight, expressionless face was worth it to keep smooth, youthful-looking skin. (Apparently, she even resisted smiling when her daughter was born! Can you imagine?)

Sometimes, when I'm slathering on my lotions and potions in the evening, I think about this woman. Not because it's a cautionary tale about vanity, but because her fear wasn't necessarily directed at the right thing. Wrinkle mythology is full of misplaced fears and misplaced faith. We treat certain habits like miracle workers and others like poison, often with evidence pointed in the opposite direction. So, instead of guessing what to do and what to avoid, I asked dermatologists to bust some wrinkle myths and misconceptions. (But as the great Oscar Wilde once said, "The truth is rarely pure and never simple.")

Myth #1: Facial expressions are the main cause of wrinkles

Let's address the aforementioned smile-averse situation. If we stop facial movement, whether it's a smile, frown or Elvis-like lip snarl, it would stop wrinkles, right? According to Dr. Behrooz Torkian , a double board-certified facial plastic surgeon based in Beverly Hills, Calif., it's not that simple. Now, some wrinkles really are caused by movement: "A prime example of this is the wrinkles on the forehead, the glabella, or so-called 'elevens,' and the crow's feet," he says. But movement is also competing with bigger forces like sun exposure and collagen loss. His advice is to limit repetitive movement with Botox where it matters, and protect collagen with adequate SPF , a good diet, stress control and no smoking.

To rebuild collagen, Torkian recommends vitamin C , retinoids , growth factors and peptides , along with regular microneedling, radio frequency and laser treatments. And if you happen to have a red light mask in your closet, now's the time to break it out. "Recent scientific evidence on red light therapy has also supported the use of red and near-infrared light to support the metabolic processes of building collagen in the skin," he says.

Myth #2: How much you wrinkle depends solely on genetics

Your bloodline may set things up for your skin, but it doesn't decide the outcome alone. "Genetics matter because your genes shape how thick your skin is, how well you hold onto collagen and how much melanin you have doing built-in sun protection," says Dr. Geeta Yadav, a board-certified dermatologist and founder of Facet Dermatology. This is part of why some people "start creasing in their 30s while others sail into their 60s looking smooth."

However, she points out how identical twins with identical DNA can look years apart in age. She underscores the sun's impact on our skin, which makes movement seem like a minor threat by comparison. "Sun alone is estimated to account for around 80% of the visible aging we see on the face," she says.

Myth #3: The more expensive the moisturizer, the better

By now, you probably know that drugstore beauty can go toe-to-toe with luxury brands , and moisture is no exception. "I have always believed that paying a lot for a moisturizer is not worth it," says Torkian. What matters, he says, is what's actually in the jar. Moisturizers break down into three parts: humectants that draw in water, emollients that soften and occlusives that seal it all in. Beyond that, you want to consider whether it has actives, such as peptides, retinoids, hydroxy acids and niacinamide. "As a general rule, I personally avoid the super expensive and the super cheap," he says.

Myth #4: Dry skin causes wrinkles; oily skin ages better

"One of the most essential factors in the appearance of wrinkles in skin is the hydration of the collagen, hyaluronic acid and elastin within the dermis and epidermis," explains Torkian. Oil definitely supports it, as more sebaceous glands mean the skin has a built-in defense system against losing that moisture. However, dry skin doesn't necessarily mean you're doomed. It just needs that same protection in a different way: "Moisturizers such as ceramides to augment the skin barrier" versus retinoids and hydroxy acids for oily skin — at least as a starting point.

According to Torkian, internal hydration is definitely a part of the picture, but only if the skin barrier is already intact and topical moisture is in place. But water alone doesn't do the plumping. A 2015 study published in Clinical, Cosmetic and Investigational Dermatology showed that adding roughly 2 liters of water a day to women's diets for a month significantly improved skin hydration and biomechanics.

Ultimately, it's less that water plumps wrinkles and more that dehydration accelerates them. Yadav is more blunt, saying that drinking more water is unlikely to meaningfully change wrinkles.

Myth #6: Retinol and tretinoin are interchangeable

Both retinol and tretinoin speed up cell turnover and rebuild collagen, which smooths and softens wrinkles over time. But the real question is which one gets you there and how fast. Torkian breaks down how tretinoin is the active compound itself, whereas retinol has to go through two steps to convert into tretinoin. "This means that using tretinoin can lead to quicker results and quicker onset of the results, but it can also feel a little bit more harsh to skin that has not adjusted to retinoic acid yet," he says. Over the long term, results from both can be very similar, he adds.

Myth #7: Only in-office procedures can reverse wrinkles, not topicals

According to Torkian, the answer to this isn't a flat no. "There are some topicals that can be very helpful in reversing wrinkling," he says, "provided that the wrinkling has not gone out of hand." Retinoids, especially prescription tretinoin, have decades of trial evidence behind them, while vitamin C, growth factors and peptides can also make a difference.

But he doesn't stop there: "Another essential factor is whether proper prevention is being employed at the same time as using the topical that is intended to reverse wrinkling." In other words, a product working solo, without sun protection or consistency, applied to wrinkles that are already deeply set isn't a fair test of what topicals can actually do.

Myth #8: The neck and chest age faster than the face

While it's true that the skin on the neck and chest is very different from the skin on the face (mainly because there are fewer oil glands), Torkian pushes back on the framing of this myth, and points out the impact of our behavior. "One thing to keep in mind about the skin of the neck and chest is that they rarely get any love," he says. "I always like to remind my patients that when they have their skin-care routine, they should not forget the neck and chest. It is natural to want to use all of your expensive skin-care products on what you feel people are looking at the most, but spreading a little love below the chin can be impactful over time in preventing neck and chest aging."

Myth #9: Botox is the best treatment for all kinds of wrinkles

Yadav is clear that Botox is excellent for softening the dynamic lines caused by repeated muscle movement. "Frown lines, forehead lines and crow's feet respond beautifully, because quieting the muscle stops it folding the skin above it thousands of times a day," she explains. But it does much less for lines already etched in when your face is completely at rest, and very little for crepey texture, sun damage or the sagging that comes from lost volume and laxity, she says.

At under $10, this effective cream is proof of Myth #3 — you don't have to splurge to get real results. It pairs retinol with bakuchiol, a plant-derived retinol alternative that helps soften irritation, plus vitamin E and allantoin to keep skin calm. You get softer-looking lines and plumper, less flakey skin without the retinol redness.

One of the most effective anti-aging treatments available without a prescription is Differin. This dermatologist favorite can help improve skin texture, fine lines and overall skin tone as long as you're consistent. It can also help build collagen, which, in turn, makes skin look brighter and bouncier.

This budget-friendly moisturizer does barrier-repair work while you sleep thanks to a powerful trio of ceramides, hyaluronic acid and peptides. It's essentially the ingredient-category cheat sheet from Myth #6 packed into an affordable cream.

We voted this the best drugstore face serum for a reason. It contains Vichy's legendary Volcanic Water, which is sourced from French volcanoes and contains 15 essential minerals that strengthen, protect and repair the skin barrier​.

This Celimax cream features a two-in-one dispenser, releasing a retinal cream with 5% panthenol soothing cream at the same time. It also explicitly treats the neck alongside the face with matrixyl 3000, a peptide complex, for firming, so you can make sure Myth #8 gets covered.

articles.title: California couple confront their surrogate in a Texas court as dispute over newborn escalates
articles.summary: DALLAS — A California couple in an escalating fight with their surrogate over a newborn with a life-threatening heart defect told a Texas court Tuesday that the child’s condition has worsened and they are anguished by attempts to deny them parental rights because they previously wanted an abortion.
articles.body: DALLAS — A California couple in an escalating fight with their surrogate over a newborn with a life-threatening heart defect told a Texas court Tuesday that the child’s condition has worsened and they are anguished by attempts to deny them parental rights because they previously wanted an abortion. “He’s our child,” Nausheen Gilkar said, wiping away tears on the witness stand. “She’s unstable,” Gilkar said of surrogate McKenna West, who was sitting across from her in the Dallas courtroom. “She’s trying to take him from us.” The hearing offered the fullest public airing to date of a deepening and high-profile dispute over surrogacy and abortion that has rushed right-to-life groups and GOP officeholders to the side of West, a nurse who flew from Alaska to have the baby on Aug. 12 in Texas, where most abortions are banned. Gilkar and her husband, Omar Ahmed, say they named the newborn Rumi. Attorneys for West, who has called the child Gabriel, said she is seeking sole conservatorship to make medical decisions for the child. It was not clear when the judge would issue an order in the case. West told the court that she was 23 weeks pregnant when she made an appointment for an abortion at the couple’s urging but was not comfortable with it. “I knew that this baby, despite the diagnosis, had a great chance at survival and a great chance at leading a long life,” West said. After West gave birth, the couple obtained a restraining order barring her from seeing or holding the child. The judge did not rule on final custody or conservatorship Tuesday, and the restraining order was left in effect. Couple say child’s condition has declined ‘significantly’ Court documents filed by the couple’s attorney prior to the hearing said Rumi was in critical condition and appeared to be “suffering from potential complications” from a procedure after he was born. The child has hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a congenital defect in which one side of the organ is underdeveloped, preventing normal blood flow. Fewer than 1,000 newborns each year have the condition, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Without treatment, death can come within days or weeks. Gilkar told the court that the baby had no blood flow to the left side of his heart. Since surgery, she said, he has gasped for air, choked on tubes and needed a blood transfusion. “He’s the most beautiful person I’ve never seen,” Gilkar said. “He’s the love of our lives. He’s suffering a lot.” Surrogate’s attorney presses couple over proposed abortion West and her attorneys have argued that Gilkar and Ahmed were not committed to guaranteeing that the baby would undergo surgeries or “life-saving care.” They say West should have conservatorship because the couple asked her to terminate the pregnancy after learning of the baby’s diagnosis. On the stand, West told their attorney, Lee Budner, that if the court finds that the couple are committed to the baby receiving the surgeries, she would drop any custody claims. Jeff Domen, an attorney for West, repeatedly pressed Gilkar on the couple’s desire to terminate the pregnancy, asking her to confirm that she requested it. Asked if she regretted the decision, Gilkar responded that she did not. “Would you trust somebody to care for your child that wanted your child dead?” Domen asked. Gilkar said she did not know how to respond to the question. Accusations that surrogate broke contract Gilkar and Ahmed say West violated the surrogacy contract they entered in August 2025. Gilkar told the court that she entered the contract after going through eight rounds of in vitro fertilization in Los Angeles and her body “gave up.” She had to undergo a hysterectomy, she said. “It was not my first choice, it was my only option,” Gilkar said. West stayed in the couple’s home in Los Angeles, Gilkar said, and she was there with West for the IVF transfer. “I was holding her hand,” Gilkar said, crying. The couple’s attorney referenced court records from California that determined West has no rights to legal or physical custody. West said she wanted the judge to disregard that ruling, saying she was willing to fight for him since the diagnosis. Surrogacy is not regulated on a federal level, and experts say each state has its own laws, which can leave room for gaps in interpretation. “We believe Ms. West is the mother of this child,” Domen said.

articles.title: Hundreds missing as flash flood sweeps villages near Nepal-Tibet border
articles.summary: Three Americans are among hundreds of people missing after torrential floods swept through the Himalayan border areas of Nepal and China’s Tibet.
articles.body: A wall of mud and rock appeared to collapse ​into a river on the Himalayan border of Nepal and China’s Tibet on Wednesday, triggering catastrophic flooding on the Nepali side that killed at least 31 people and left ‌hundreds of tourists missing. In a still-unfolding disaster, verified videos showed dozens of people swept away at the border, with authorities on both sides fearing far higher casualties and massive destruction. Houses, roads and power projects were swept away in Nepal, while officials in Tibet said they feared “major casualties” with some missing in the county of Gyirong after a mudslide hit a border land crossing. Initial reports suggested that an earthquake in the area could have triggered an avalanche and caused the floods, ​Nepal’s foreign minister Shisir Khanal told the country’s parliament on Wednesday, local media reported. At least 384 travellers, including 105 Indians, 93 Nepalis, three U.S. citizens and 12 British nationals were missing ​from the region, Nepal’s tourism authority said. South Korean news agency Yonhap separately reported that about eight of its nationals were also unaccounted for in Nepal. Flood ⁠alerts were issued in the populous northern Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar as they border Nepal and several rivers flow down the mountains into their plains. Experts fear a second flood Security footage captured ​on the Chinese side of the Nepal-Tibet border showed many people fleeing before a wall of rock, mud and water destroyed buildings, vehicles and took many lives. The exact cause of the mudslide could not be ​immediately determined, but the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said there was a 4.4 magnitude quake approximately seven minutes before the time shown on the security footage time-stamp. An ice-rock avalanche in the Lhende Khola river on the Nepali side was the trigger, but the cause remains unconfirmed, said Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks, at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development. “With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood ​may occur,” Qianggong said. Rescue helicopters could not land in Nepal’s affected areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa, with a population of about 50,000, officials said, with the river flowing above its normal course. Television broadcast images of crumbled homes in the floodwaters, floating cars and a metal bridge being washed away, while witnesses told Reuters the waters engulfed entire villages. “There could be heavy casualties or loss of property,” said district administrator Narendra Pariyar, who urged dwellers on the banks of the Bhote Koshi river to move to higher ground, after reports of villages and project sites being swept up. “There is devastation everywhere we look,” Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa, told Reuters. “The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.” Nepal’s rescue helicopters would be unable to land in the affected areas until the waters recede, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said. The cause of the inundation was not immediately clear, but a deadly flash flood on the same river last year was eventually traced to the draining of a glacier lake. China’s official Xinhua news agency said the mudslide occurred on the Nepali side and hit the Gyirong port to cut roads, communications and power links in the Shigatse region near the border with Nepal, but did not elaborate. President Xi Jinping urged “all-out” search efforts for the missing as well as stronger monitoring and early warning systems to prevent secondary disasters. Nepal’s energy ministry said 430 MW of electricity supplies were affected, mostly from hydroelectric projects, or more than 12% of total national hydropower capacity of 3.2 GW, a Reuters calculation showed. Police and military were joining in the rescue effort, said Prime Minister Balendra Shah. “Instructions have been given ... to move the people living in the lower areas to safer places,” he said. “People along the river are advised to exercise extra caution and remain alert.” From its origins in Tibet, the Bhote Koshi river empties into Nepal’s Trishuli river that eventually flows into India as the Gandak river. Last year’s Bhote Koshi flood killed nine people, with 24 missing, as it washed away a “Friendship Bridge” linking Nepal and China to disrupt trade and transport for months. That flood was triggered by the draining of a supraglacial lake in Tibet, a regional climate monitor said.

articles.title: Photos: Thousands join Spain’s La Tomatina festival for epic tomato battle
articles.summary: About 20,000 participants hurled 165 tonnes of tomatoes in Bunol’s streets during Spain’s famed La Tomatina festival.
articles.body:
Thousands of revellers have packed into the narrow streets of Buñol in eastern Spain for La Tomatina, the town’s annual tomato-throwing festival that has become one of the country’s most distinctive summer attractions.

For about an hour on Wednesday, trucks unloaded up to 165 tonnes of overripe tomatoes into the crowd as festival-goers, many in white T-shirts, hurled the fruit at each other to a soundtrack of blasting pop music.

Authorities covered buildings with tarps before the melee and deployed police, who at one point appeared to use pepper spray to disperse part of the crowd before the festivities quickly resumed.

More than 20,000 people were expected to attend, with Spanish media reporting that about 40 percent of participants in recent years are international tourists, including a growing number from India following the 2011 Bollywood film Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara.

La Tomatina, held on the last Wednesday of August, began with a local food fight in 1945 and survived a ban under Francisco Franco before television turned it into a global spectacle.

articles.title: Tom Byabagamba: Ex-head of Rwandan President Paul Kagame's presidential guard dies in jail 12 years after his arrest
articles.summary: His brother tells the BBC his family have not been allowed to see him "in all these years".
articles.body:
Former head of Rwanda's presidential guard Tom Byabagamba, 59, who once served as President Paul Kagame's personal bodyguard, has died in jail.

He was arrested in 2014 along with his brother-in-law Frank Rusagara, a retired brigadier-general, for "spreading rumours" and "tarnishing the image of the country and government".

Right groups expressed concern over their cases, framing them as a part of a pattern of government repression. Throughout his trial, Col Byabagamba denied the allegations against him, saying they were fabricated.

Byabagamba's brother David Himbara told the BBC Great Lakes service his family did not know the cause of death as "no-one was allowed to see him in all these years".

Rights groups have repeatedly accused Kagame's government of restricting political opposition and silencing critics within Rwanda and abroad.

In 2016, a military court convicted Byagamba and imprisoned him for 21 years, although this was later reduced to 15 years on appeal. Rusagara, who had also been secretary-general of the defence ministry, was given a 20-year sentence.

Rusagara died in prison in March last year. At the time Human Rights Watch (HRW) described it as the "lonely death of a general", noting that his family had not heard his voice since 2014, days before his arrest.

His family was informed by the authorities that Rusagara had been ill with cancer, the rights group said.

The conviction of the two men had followed a "flawed trial" marked by "serious allegations of torture and witness tampering", according to HRW.

Campaign group Freedom Now had also previously criticised their detention as "arbitrary" and as having "violated international law".

Byabagamba leaves behind two sons and a wife.

articles.title: In 2018, Florida opened Americaâs first permanent underwater sculpture garden 58 feet below the Gulf; it has grown into a living reef where more than 100 species have been documented
articles.summary: US News: Imagine you are diving under the Gulf of Mexico and come upon what looks like a museum, only instead of galleries and polished floors, there is an unr.
articles.body: Imagine you are diving under the Gulf of Mexico and come upon what looks like a museum, only instead of galleries and polished floors, there is an unreal world of sculptures, tropical fish and drifting sea life. Florida's Underwater Museum of Art has turned the ocean floor into a gallery at 58 feet below the surface, where art is slowly becoming part of nature. Located about 0.93 miles off the shore of Grayton Beach State Park in Walton County, the Underwater Museum of Art (UMA) is the first permanent underwater sculpture garden in the United States. But it is more than an unusual destination for divers. Its sculptures have been designed specifically to be artificial reefs, creating habitat on an area dominated by barren sand. Scroll down to read the details.Art Meets the GulfAccording to its official website, the museum was a collaboration between the Cultural Arts Alliance of Walton County and the South Walton Artificial Reef Association in 2018. The idea was simple, but ambitious: merge artistic expression with marine conservation. Artists from around the country and the world are invited to submit sculptures for consideration each year. Selected works are engineered, transported and carefully positioned on the sea bed. They are built to endure a harsh environment and to support marine life, not conventional museum pieces. Artists and organizers must meet certain requirements for materials, structural integrity and ecological safety, including requirements that allow sea turtles to escape safely if they become trapped. The result is an ever-changing underwater gallery.A museum that turns into a reefThe sculptures are not just objects that are submerged in water. They become living structures in time. Here, artificial reefs offer surfaces and shelter for fish, invertebrates and other marine organisms. The structures can offer cover and breeding habitat for small creatures, and the baitfish attract larger predators. Juvenile fish can also take shelter as they grow. That ecological role is especially vital in Walton County, where much of the Gulfâs coastal seafloor is open sand flats.Since the museum opened, more than 100 species of marine and plant life have been recorded around the sculptures. Dolphins and sea turtles, along with a range of fish and invertebrates, are also found. For scientists, the site offers more than a beautiful underwater landscape. It offers an opportunity to monitor the development of artificial reef systems and their potential impacts on marine environments.A gallery of odd and wonderful artThe sculptures vary from playful to monumental. One of them is âPoseidonâs Throneâ, which is at once a symbolic seat of power and habitat for marine organisms. âA Common Chordâ takes the form of a giant guitar, and celebrates the relationship between humans and nature. Other installations are âThree Wishes,â a genie lamp that divers can play with by blowing air into small openings, and âI Found It,â a giant diamond ring lying on the Gulf floor. A giant octopus, a skull, a seashell and a pirate shipwreck augment the otherworldly atmosphere. The works together form a landscape that is part art exhibition and part sunken fantasy and part thriving ecosystem.A laboratory of life below the seaUMA has drawn in divers and art lovers, as well as marine scientists, ecologists, wildlife professionals and students. Researchers can observe artificial structures transform into working habitats as the sculptures slowly get colonized by marine organisms. It is therefore both an ecotourism attraction and an ongoing experiment in the conservation of the marine environment. The project has also garnered international attention, being featured by major media outlets and recognized as a notable travel destination.Exploring the underwater museumThe museum is free for scuba divers but you need proper diving experience to get there. Visitors must be qualified divers and comfortable with open sea conditions. Dive excursions range from the coast near Grayton Beach State Park to the submerged site, where visitors can explore the sculptures and the marine life that has made them home. What started as a curious collaboration between artists and conservationists in 2018 has morphed into something much more interesting: a museum that changes every year. Its sculptures may have been carved by humans but down under the Gulf, nature is also dabbling in art.Images Courtesy: Underwater Museum of ArtCatch the latest World News and Live updates.
